title: File uploads

spans.text: WHY USE THIS?
FastAPI builds JSON APIs that web and mobile applications call over HTTP; type annotations help validate inputs and describe the API contract.
PURPOSE AND REAL-WORLD USE

An upload endpoint accepts `UploadFile` through multipart; the client controls the filename and MIME type, so do not trust them. This example reads at most 1 MiB and does not write to disk. Install `fastapi uvicorn httpx python-multipart`.

To run these examples locally, install `pip install fastapi uvicorn httpx` plus any extra package named in the lesson. Save the server example as `app.py` and start `uvicorn app:app --reload`. `--reload` is for development only.

WHERE DOES THIS APPEAR IN REAL LIFE?
A lesson endpoint accepts a small text file, checks its size and client-declared MIME type, and does not persist it.
If this part is omitted: Without size limits, a large body can consume resources; without content inspection, a misleading file type may be accepted.

REQUEST AND EXPECTED RESPONSE

spans.code:
Request: POST /upload  multipart file=<small text file>
Response: 200 JSON `{size: N, content_type: ...}`; the demo does not persist the file.

spans.text:
LINE-BY-LINE CODE EXPLANATION
`from fastapi import FastAPI, File, HTTPException, UploadFile` — Imports a required type or tool; without it, the name is unavailable.
`app = FastAPI()` — `FastAPI()` creates the ASGI application that holds the routes and is passed to the server.
`MAX_BYTES = 1024 * 1024` — Continues the application's data handling or control flow.
`@app.post("/upload")` — Binds an HTTP method and URL path to this function; without the decorator, it is not an API endpoint.
`async def upload(file: UploadFile = File(...)):` — Defines the endpoint the server calls; parameter names help bind path, query, or body data.
`contents = await file.read(MAX_BYTES + 1)` — Waits for an asynchronous I/O operation; without `await`, the value may only be a coroutine.
`if len(contents) > MAX_BYTES:` — Chooses a branch when the condition is true and handles an edge case.
`raise HTTPException(status_code=413, detail="File too large")` — Stops the request with an explicit status and error detail instead of hiding the failure.
`if file.content_type != "text/plain":` — Chooses a branch when the condition is true and handles an edge case.
`raise HTTPException(status_code=415, detail="Only text files are accepted")` — Stops the request with an explicit status and error detail instead of hiding the failure.
`return {"size": len(contents), "content_type": file.content_type}` — Returns the HTTP response value; FastAPI converts it to JSON and applies the response model.
PRACTICE: CHECK IT WITH AN HTTP CLIENT
This complete file calls the app locally with TestClient; it does not open a server port. Install `httpx` for TestClient.
COMPLETE RUNNABLE CLIENT TEST
QUESTION: What will this code print? Predict first, then run it.

spans.code:
from fastapi import FastAPI, File, HTTPException, UploadFile

app = FastAPI()
MAX_BYTES = 1024 * 1024

@app.post("/upload")
async def upload(file: UploadFile = File(...)):
    contents = await file.read(MAX_BYTES + 1)
    if len(contents) > MAX_BYTES:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=413, detail="File too large")
    if file.content_type != "text/plain":
        raise HTTPException(status_code=415, detail="Only text files are accepted")
    return {"size": len(contents), "content_type": file.content_type}

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

with TestClient(app) as client:
    response = client.post("/upload", files={"file": ("note.txt", b"hello", "text/plain")})
    print(response.status_code, response.json())

`raise HTTPException(status_code=413, detail="File too large")` — Stops the request with an explicit status and error detail instead of hiding the failure.

COMMON MISTAKES
Joining `filename` directly into a path or trusting `content_type`; sanitize names and inspect content.

spans.title: Practical tip
spans.text: Set compatible upload-size limits at the proxy, API, and application layers.

spans.title: One level deeper
spans.text: `UploadFile` can spool large files, but a parser or proxy may receive the body first; endpoint checks alone are not enough.

spans.title: Important warning
spans.text: Never use a client filename as a server path; separately handle malicious content, oversize files, and archive bombs.
QUICK RECALL
Question: Which action best prevents the common mistake from this lesson?
Answer: Set compatible upload-size limits at the proxy, API, and application layers.
